name: The Eastern Woodlands
covers: Eastern US: deciduous forest, creek bottoms, old farmland (today's game)

climate._note: Seasons from biomes.json se_woodlands (365 days). Every season carries today's one global roll (clear .7 / rain .2 / cold .1) so the migration changes nothing; a seasonal table is a CONTENT change.

seasons.note: Greens return. Hungry season ends — if you make it.
Berries, heat, snakes. Water is everywhere; food takes work.
Harvest season. Nuts, persimmons, last greens. Fatten up.
The boss. Nuts and stored food or nothing. Game gets bold.

fauna._note: Real eastern-US species only (Steve 2026-10-14: trim approved). Western and plains animals live in their own regions (bison/pronghorn/prairie dog -> na_plains; javelina/roadrunner/gila monster -> na_arid; elk/spotted owl/moose/snowshoe hare -> na_boreal_pacific). variants: a landing variant (locations.json id) adds its own animals: alligator and nutria in the southern swamps, moose and snowshoe hare in the northern marsh and beaver country. Florida panther and Burmese python wait for a Florida (Everglades) landing.

creekside grove: Riparian ground. Water means life, and lunch.
deep grove: Mast country. The old trees feed everything.
orchard ruin: Someone planted food here once. The trees remember.
creek meadow: Open ground by water — the onion beds.
creek bend: Slow water. The cattails stand thick.
creekmouth marsh: Where the creek spreads out, the starch grows.
edge thicket: Edge habitat. Berries grow where the light gets in.
the old trail: Trampled ground. The humble weeds win.
forest floor: Deep shade. The floor keeps its secrets.

ruins: A collapsed barn. Pre-Burn. The wiring is gone — everything is gone — but the stones remember the shape of work.
A farmhouse foundation. Someone's kitchen. The Burn took the wires from the walls; the walls kept standing out of spite.
A gas station. The pumps are sculptures now. Nothing combustible within miles — the Burn was thorough.

scavenge.name: Canned beans
scavenge.text: Dusty can, intact seal. Someone's pantry, a lifetime ago.

scavenge.name: Machete
scavenge.text: Under the pantry shelf, wrapped in oilcloth: a machete, edge still bright. Whoever lived here cleared brush — and problems.

scavenge.name: Leather jacket
scavenge.text: A leather jacket on a hook by the door, stiff with age. It smells like someone else's life — and it stops teeth better than skin does.

scavenge.name: Canned corn
scavenge.text: The label is gone. The corn doesn't care.

scavenge.name: Canned soup
scavenge.text: Chicken soup. Tastes like before.

scavenge.name: Jarred peaches
scavenge.text: Home-canned. Whoever sealed this knew what they were doing.

scavenge.name: Antibiotics (amoxicillin)
scavenge.text: A rattling bottle, seal intact. For bacterial infections. Read the label.

scavenge.name: Antiparasitic (mebendazole)
scavenge.text: Foil blister pack, unbroken. For worms and gut parasites. Only for those.

scavenge.name: Futures Ledger
scavenge.text: A water-stained ledger in a dry box, its last pages filled with careful columns of debts and promises.

scavenge.name: Oath Ring
scavenge.text: A plain ring on a cord, hung by the door where someone would see it every morning.

scavenge.name: Trail Rations Pouch
scavenge.text: A waxed pouch, still buckled, the kind a careful walker packs the night before.

scavenge.name: Memory Lantern
scavenge.text: A lantern with a note wired to the handle: 'For remembering the way back.'

scavenge.name: Hatchet
scavenge.text: A hatchet hung by the back door, edge still keen. Made for splitting kindling — and for felling what needs felling.

challenge.name: The Long Winter
challenge.description: No single killer. Winter is the boss — stockpile or starve.

seedData.name: Middle America
seedData.description: Rolling deciduous forest, creek bottoms, old farmland edges. Four real seasons. The baseline — balanced, forgiving, familiar. This is the game's default setting.

asOrigin.culture: Corn-fed practicality. You grew up knowing which berries won't kill you and that winter is the real boss. Food is something you work for, not something you're given.

challenge.name: The Long Winter
challenge.description: No single killer. Winter is the boss — stockpile or starve.

monsters.name: Corn Mother
monsters.concept: A harvest spirit wearing a dress of dried husks. She walks the field rows at dusk, and where she steps, the corn grows wrong — too fast, too tall, with teeth. She is not angry. She is disappointed you stopped farming.
monsters.behaviorHook: Territorial around meadows/farmland tiles. Her 'harvest' attack reaps in a wide arc.

monsters.name: The Combiner
monsters.concept: An agricultural machine that kept working after the drivers left. It has combined itself with three other machines and something that used to be a deer. It harvests everything — corn, trees, houses, people. The System finds it efficient.
monsters.behaviorHook: Charge-pattern like Bulldozer but wider. Drops machine parts as loot.

asHaven.strategy: Generalist survival. Diverse food sources, stockpile for winter. The balanced start — learn the game's systems here before the regions get mean.

seasons.spring: Greens return. Morels if you know where to look. Hungry season ends — if you make it.
seasons.summer: Berries, heat, snakes. Water is everywhere; food takes work.
seasons.fall: Harvest season. Nuts, persimmons, pawpaws. Fatten up.
seasons.winter: The boss. Nuts and stored food or nothing. Game gets bold.

seedData.name: Appalachian
seedData.description: Dense hardwood forest, steep hollers, clean mountain water. The terrain is the challenge — everything is uphill, and the hollers hide food and danger in equal measure.

asOrigin.culture: Holler-raised. You know ramps from skunk cabbage and ginseng from Virginia creeper. The mountains taught you that everything worth having is uphill, and everything dangerous is quiet.

challenge.name: The Hollers
challenge.description: Clean water, hard ground. The mountains don't care about you. Elevation is everything — food, safety, and escape all depend on knowing the terrain.

monsters.name: Hollow Voice
monsters.concept: A mountain echo predator. It throws its voice — you hear it behind you, above you, inside the holler walls. By the time you find it, it's already somewhere else.
monsters.behaviorHook: Misdirection. Auditory telegraphs that lie about position.

monsters.name: The Company
monsters.concept: A coal company phantom — a foreman with a lamp that never goes out, still collecting. It offers you a job. The pay is your name.
monsters.behaviorHook: Bargain/contract mechanic. Thematically about extraction and debt.

asHaven.strategy: Elevation is everything. Ridges for travel, hollers for food, creeks for water. The forest is dense but generous if you know it. Don't trust echoes.

seasons.spring: Ramps. Morels. The hollers wake up hungry.
seasons.summer: Thick and green. Berries in the clearings. Snakes on the rocks.
seasons.fall: Mast crop — acorns, hickory, beech. The bears know. You should too.
seasons.winter: Quiet. The mountains hold their breath. Game comes to the creeks.

seedData.name: Deep South Bayou
seedData.description: Cypress swamp, black water, Spanish moss. Water is everywhere and it's all trying to give you something — usually a disease. The gators were here first and they know it.

asOrigin.culture: You learned to read water like a book — what's under it, what's in it, what it'll do to you. You boil everything, you respect the gators, and you know that the swamp provides for those who don't fight it.

challenge.name: The Black Water
challenge.description: Contamination and disease. The water gives — crawfish, cattails, fish — and the water takes. Everything must be cooked, boiled, or avoided.

monsters.name: Swamp Thing
monsters.concept: A cypress amalgam — roots, knees, moss, and something that used to be a boat. It rises from the black water when the swamp is disturbed. It is the swamp, defending itself.

monsters.name: The Hymn
monsters.concept: A drowned choir. You hear the singing before you see anything — old spirituals in too many voices, coming from under the water. It wants you to join.
monsters.behaviorHook: Sonic/charm effects. Thematically about the bayou's drowned history.

asHaven.strategy: Stay dry. Boil everything. Respect the gators — they're not monsters, they're neighbors. The swamp rewards those who move slow and watch the water.

seasons.spring: High water. Everything floods. The swamp reclaims.
seasons.summer: Heat, humidity, mosquitoes. The air is soup.
seasons.fall: Crawfish season. The water drops. Best foraging.
seasons.winter: Mild. The gators slow down. The only easy season.

seedData.name: Florida
seedData.description: Heat, humidity, hurricanes. Water everywhere but it's brackish. Everything is trying to rot, including you. The pythons weren't invited but they're here now.

asOrigin.culture: You grew up checking for gators before swimming and knowing that hurricane season is just... season. You know the palmetto berries are food, the water needs boiling twice, and that the python problem is everyone's problem now.

challenge.name: The Rot and the Storm
challenge.description: Heat, humidity, hurricanes. Everything rots — food, gear, wounds. Water is everywhere but brackish. The storms don't warn twice.

monsters.name: Hurricane Eye
monsters.concept: A storm entity — the calm center of something that wants to unmake you. It moves slow and certain. The wind goes still before it arrives, and that's how you know.

monsters.name: The Python King
monsters.concept: Twenty feet of invasive muscle that learned to think. It was someone's pet, then it was everyone's problem, then it was the apex. It remembers being in a tank.
monsters.behaviorHook: Constriction/grapple. Thematic about invasive species and human hubris.

asHaven.strategy: Stay high, stay dry, watch the sky. Preserve food aggressively — it rots fast. The water is not your friend (brackish). Gators are manageable; pythons are not.

seasons.spring: Dry season ends. Storms build. The pythons breed.
seasons.summer: Hurricane season. Heat index lethal. Everything rots.
seasons.fall: Storm peak, then relief. Best foraging after the storms pass.
seasons.winter: The 'cold' snap (60s). The only comfortable season. Gators slow down.

seedData.name: Northeast
seedData.description: Maple-beech forest, cold lakes, granite. Winter doesn't negotiate — it takes. The growing season is short, the woods are deep, and preparation is the difference between life and death.

asOrigin.culture: You grew up stacking wood in September because October is too late. You know that winter is not a season — it's a siege. Maple sap runs when the days thaw and the nights freeze, and you know it in your bones.

challenge.name: The Deep Cold
challenge.description: Winter doesn't negotiate. The growing season is short. Prepare from day one or the cold takes you — slowly, then all at once.

monsters.name: Winter
monsters.concept: Personified cold. Not a creature — a season that learned to walk. It doesn't chase you. It just arrives, and then you're making decisions about which fingers you need.
monsters.behaviorHook: Cold/exposure damage aura. The fight is about shelter, not strength.

monsters.name: The Loon's Call
monsters.concept: A lake entity that sounds like a loon — until you realize loons don't call in winter, and this is coming from under the ice. It remembers everyone who ever drowned in its lake.
monsters.behaviorHook: Lure to water/ice. Thematic about the lakes' hidden depths.

asHaven.strategy: Prepare for winter from day one. Every fall action should ask: 'will this keep me alive in January?' Moose are food and death. The lakes give fish but take the careless.

seasons.spring: Mud season. Sap run. The world thaws and everything is urgent.
seasons.summer: Short and intense. Berries, fish, blackflies. Make hay.
seasons.fall: The countdown. Mast crop, moose rut, last chance to prepare.
seasons.winter: The siege. Deep snow, deep cold. You live on what you stored.

fauna._note: Stub fauna (moved from the eastern woodlands 2026-10-14 plus shared plains species). Not playable yet.

seedData.name: Great Plains
seedData.description: Open grassland to the horizon. Few trees, big sky, bigger wind. Fire is the constant threat — the grass wants to burn, and when it does, it runs faster than you.

asOrigin.culture: You grew up with the horizon in every direction. You can read weather in the clouds an hour out. You know fire the way sailors know the sea — with respect, because you've seen what it does.

challenge.name: The Fire Season
challenge.description: Wildfire is the constant threat. The grass wants to burn. When the wind shifts, you run — and you'd better know which way.

monsters.name: Prairie Fire
monsters.concept: A living wildfire spirit — not the fire itself, but the hunger behind it. It moves with the wind, and it remembers every firebreak you build.
monsters.behaviorHook: Spreading area damage. Wind-direction mechanic. Firebreaks as counterplay.

monsters.name: The Twister
monsters.concept: A tornado that thinks. It doesn't just destroy — it hunts, circling, probing, looking for the ones who run. The sky goes green before it comes.
monsters.behaviorHook: Massive area attack with telegraphed path. The ultimate 'don't be there' monster.

asHaven.strategy: Firebreaks and mobility. Keep the grass short around camp. Watch the sky — weather kills here faster than monsters. Bison are food and danger in equal measure.

seasons.spring: Green-up. Tornado season. Watch the sky.
seasons.summer: Fire season. The grass cures to tinder. Everything is fuel.
seasons.fall: Harvest. Bison move. The wind turns cold.
seasons.winter: Blizzards. White-out. The fire sleeps but the cold doesn't.

fauna._note: Stub fauna (moved from the eastern woodlands 2026-10-14 plus shared Southwest species). Not playable yet.

seedData.name: Southwest Desert
seedData.description: Red rock, scrub, and sky. Water is the biggest issue — every drop counts. Extreme heat by day, cold by night. Flash floods in monsoon season. The land is beautiful and trying to kill you.

asOrigin.culture: You learned young that water is life and shade is survival. You can read the sky for rain three days out. You know which cactus won't kill you and that the desert gives — but only to the patient.

challenge.name: The Thirst
challenge.description: Water is the biggest issue. Creeks are dry washes. Every drop must be found, cached, or coaxed from the land.

monsters.name: Dust Devil
monsters.concept: A living dust storm, vaguely humanoid, that wanders the washes. It doesn't hate you — it doesn't notice you, the way you don't notice ants. Getting noticed is the problem.
monsters.behaviorHook: Area-denial. Its dust cloud blinds and chokes. Don't fight it in the open.

monsters.name: The Mirage
monsters.concept: It shows you water. A spring, a creek, a full canteen — always just over the next ridge. People have died following it. The System classifies it as 'interactive art.'
monsters.behaviorHook: Lure/ambush predator. Thematically tied to the water-scarcity challenge — it weaponizes hope.

asHaven.strategy: Cache water. Travel at night, rest in shade by day. Prickly pear is food AND water. The desert rewards patience and punishes haste.

seasons.spring: Brief bloom. Everything flowers at once. Beautiful and short.
seasons.summer: The furnace. Travel at night or not at all. Monsoon storms bring flash floods.
seasons.fall: Relief. Prickly pear fruits ripen. The land exhales.
seasons.winter: Cold nights, mild days. The easiest season — which isn't saying much.

name: The Pacific Rainforest and the North

fauna._note: Stub fauna (moved from the eastern woodlands 2026-10-14 plus shared northern species). Not playable yet.

seedData.name: Pacific Northwest
seedData.description: Dense evergreen forest, constant rain, moss on everything. Water is everywhere — and none of it is safe. The forest provides abundantly but hides its dangers in the green.

asOrigin.culture: You grew up damp. You know that everything here is either food, medicine, or trying to give you giardia. You can tell a salmonberry from a thimbleberry at fifty paces and you distrust any water you didn't boil yourself.

challenge.name: The Green Water
challenge.description: Water everywhere, none of it safe. Giardia, runoff, rot. Purification isn't optional — it's the whole game.

monsters.name: Old Growth
monsters.concept: An ancient tree that decided to walk. It moves inches per day, but it remembers every axe. It doesn't chase — it waits. You will come to it.
monsters.behaviorHook: Ambush predator disguised as terrain. Thematically about the forest's memory.

monsters.name: The Fog
monsters.concept: Sentient mist that rolls in off the water. People walk into it and walk out different — or don't walk out. It shows you things in the grey.
monsters.behaviorHook: Disorientation/confusion effects. Visibility mechanic tied to the region's rain/fog.

asHaven.strategy: Purify everything. The forest is generous — berries, elk, salmon — but the water will kill you as fast as any monster. Fire is hard to keep in the rain; learn to love the damp.

seasons.spring: The melt. Creeks run high. Everything is mud.
seasons.summer: The dry-ish season. Berries everywhere. Best hunting.
seasons.fall: Salmon run. Mushrooms. The forest feeds you if you know how to ask.
seasons.winter: Dark and wet. Not cold enough to freeze, just cold enough to rot.

challenge.description: The river rises every year and takes the low ground for months. Game disperses, trails drown, and the water you drink wants to give you something. You don't beat the flood — you move with it, or you don't eat.
challenge.name: A Cheia (The Flood)

covers: Amazon basin: várzea floodplain, terra firme upland forest, blackwater creeks

blackwater creek: Still black water. The giant lilies spread their pads.
flooded grove: The floodplain palms stand in black water. Açaí and bacaba.
old roça: An old garden clearing. Manioc gone wild — bitter and sweet, and only knowledge tells them apart.
river beach: Sand and sun. Tucumã palms lean over the water.
terra firme rise: High ground, old giants. The castanheiras drop their cannonball pods here.
the gap: Light got in. Someone's old clearing — banana and papaya.
understory shade: Dim and damp. Cacao pods hang straight from the trunks.

name: The Amazon

ruins: A feira — the riverside market. The stalls are skeletons now, awnings rotted to lace. Nothing worth stealing; everything worth eating is long gone.
An escola, paint peeling in the humidity. The chalkboard still has a date on it. Nobody loots a school — you take a desk for firewood and feel bad about it.
A rodoviária, the bus depot. The buses rust where they died, and the timetables have faded to ghosts.

scavenge.name: Manioc flour (farinha)
scavenge.text: A sealed bag of toasted manioc flour. The Amazon's bread — bland, filling, eternal.

scavenge.name: Machete
scavenge.text: A facão leaning by the doorframe, the river people's answer to every question the forest asks. The edge has eaten a thousand vines.

scavenge.name: Bark armor
scavenge.text: Bark lashed with vine, hung on a peg like it was taken off yesterday. Better than skin — the forest teaches that fast.

scavenge.name: Canned sardines
scavenge.text: Dusty tin, intact. The river towns ran on these.

scavenge.name: Rapadura sugar blocks
scavenge.text: Hard brown bricks of raw cane sugar. A shaving in water is a meal's worth of energy.

scavenge.name: Carne-seca (dried beef)
scavenge.text: Salt-cured, sun-dried beef. Tough as a boot, keeps like a stone.

scavenge.name: Dried pirarucu
scavenge.text: Strips of the great river fish, salted and sun-dried. Chewy, salty, perfect.

scavenge.name: Guaraná powder
scavenge.text: A small bag of bitter brown powder. A pinch in water wakes you like a slap — the river people's coffee.

scavenge.name: Canned feijoada
scavenge.text: Black beans and pork, ready to eat. Tastes like before.

scavenge.name: Bag of salt
scavenge.text: Coarse salt in a tied sack. Worth its weight in everything.

scavenge.name: Antibiotics (amoxicillin)
scavenge.text: A rattling bottle from the health post's cabinet. For bacterial infections. Read the label.

scavenge.name: Antiparasitic (mebendazole)
scavenge.text: Foil blister pack, unbroken. The river gives worms with everything else. Only for those.

scavenge.name: Seedkeeper's Grimoire
scavenge.text: A seed-keeper's book wrapped in palm fiber, every page a planting and a prayer.

scavenge.name: Toxin Library
scavenge.text: Stoppered vials and a handwritten index of river poisons, labeled in a steady hand.

scavenge.name: Worldseed Satchel
scavenge.text: A satchel of sorted seeds, each packet named for the garden it was meant to start.

scavenge.name: Whispering Compass
scavenge.text: A compass whose needle trembles toward the river, not north, as if listening.

scavenge.name: Hatchet
scavenge.text: A hatchet hung by the back door, edge still keen. Made for splitting kindling — and for felling what needs felling.

challenge.description: Winter ends, but the forest doesn't get the memo. March and April are the killing months — the stores are empty, the greens aren't up yet, and the game is lean. The hungry gap.
challenge.name: Przednówek — The Hungry Gap

covers: Central Europe: beech-oak forest, creek valleys, allotment edges, and quiet ruins

beech mast grove: Mast country. The old beeches feed everything.
elder thicket: Cook the black clusters. The bush insists.
garlic bank: The whole bank smells of it in April. Sniff every leaf.
hazel coppice: Cut and regrown for a hundred years. The stools are older than the village.
mushroom hollow: Damp and dim. The mushrooms know.
oak hollow: The oaks drop dinner — if you leach it right.
old orchard: Someone planted food here once. The trees remember.
porcini ground: Where the roots run deep. Check the stems for the white net.
rose tangle: Thorns with a vitamin C pension.

name: Temperate Europe

ruins: A village school. The desks still stand in rows. Someone chalked the date of the last lesson on the board and underlined it twice.
A bus depot. The timetable behind cracked glass still lists routes to towns that aren't there anymore. A driver's lunchbox sits empty on the bench.
A corner clinic. The waiting-room chairs face a faded poster about flu shots. The medicine cabinet was emptied long ago — by someone careful, not someone desperate.
An allotment garden colony. The sheds lean and the fences sag, but someone's roses still bloom on schedule, for no one.

scavenge.name: Pickled cucumbers
scavenge.text: Dill and garlic in cloudy brine — that's how you know they're real.

scavenge.name: Crowbar
scavenge.text: A crowbar in the cellar corner, paint worn where hands gripped it for years. Opens doors. Ends arguments.

scavenge.name: Riot gear
scavenge.text: Police surplus in a mildewed kit bag. Heavy, hot, stops a boar — the tag is still in Deutsch.

scavenge.name: Dense rye loaf
scavenge.text: Stale enough to build with. Soak it and it's bread again.

scavenge.name: Canned sauerkraut
scavenge.text: Sour, salty, and full of the vitamins winter steals.

scavenge.name: Jar of honey
scavenge.text: Crystallized solid. Honey doesn't spoil; it just waits.

scavenge.name: Dried porcini
scavenge.text: Strung on a thread by someone who knew their mushrooms. Trust the string.

scavenge.name: Chocolate bar
scavenge.text: A little gray with bloom. Still chocolate.

scavenge.name: Canned white sausage
scavenge.text: The label promises Munich; the contents promise calories.

scavenge.name: Pickled beets
scavenge.text: Earthy and sweet. The jar sealed before the Burn and never looked back.

scavenge.name: Antibiotics (amoxicillin)
scavenge.text: A rattling bottle, seal intact. For bacterial infections. Read the label.

scavenge.name: Antiparasitic (mebendazole)
scavenge.text: Foil blister pack, unbroken. For worms and gut parasites. Only for those.

scavenge.name: Broker's Seal
scavenge.text: A brass seal in a desk drawer, heavy enough to end arguments about ownership.

scavenge.name: Confessional Seal
scavenge.text: A small seal in a velvet pouch, kept where private things were kept.

scavenge.name: Sanctuary Bell
scavenge.text: A hand bell wrapped in cloth, so it would not ring until someone meant it to.

scavenge.name: Horizon Compass
scavenge.text: A surveyor's compass in a fitted case, the glass uncracked.

scavenge.name: Hatchet
scavenge.text: A hatchet hung by the back door, edge still keen. Made for splitting kindling — and for felling what needs felling.

name: The Mediterranean
covers: Med basin incl. coastal N. Africa

challenge.description: No single killer. The long dry is the boss — the waterholes shrink, the grain runs out, and everything hungry gets bold.
challenge.name: The Long Dry

covers: West/East Africa savanna: baobab parkland, tall grass, riverine wetlands

baobab hollow: The old tree feeds everything that can reach.
dry riverbed: Where the water stood, the grain remembers.
old field: Someone farmed here. The millet stayed.
tamarind shade: Cool ground, sour pods. Rest and eat.
thorn scrub: Grey bush, sweet berries. The children's harvest.

name: The Sahel and the Savanna

ruins: A roadside market. Stalls in rows under a skeleton of awning poles, a painted price board that outlived money itself. The Burn took the wiring; the bargaining echoes stayed.
A village school block. Three classrooms, one blackboard with the last lesson still on it, half-erased by rain. The desks went to firewood years ago.
A rural clinic. White paint, a red cross weathered to pink. The medicine cabinet was emptied a long time ago — but check the drawers anyway. Quietly.

scavenge.name: Sack of pearl millet
scavenge.text: A torn grain sack, half-full. The millet is dry and clean — someone stored it right.

scavenge.name: Hunting spear
scavenge.text: A hunting spear racked above the lintel, stone tip wrapped in sinew. On the savanna, this was never decoration.

scavenge.name: Bark armor
scavenge.text: Bark lashed with vine, cured hard as a shield. Somebody's grandfather wore this against things with teeth.

scavenge.name: Sack of sorghum
scavenge.text: Sorghum in a woven sack. Heavy, honest, and still good.

scavenge.name: Tinned sardines
scavenge.text: Small oily fish in a tin with a faded label. The Sahel ate these by the million.

scavenge.name: Dried tilapia
scavenge.text: Sun-dried fish, stiff as boards. Soak it, stew it — the river's savings account.

scavenge.name: Bag of groundnuts
scavenge.text: Roasted groundnuts in a cloth bag. Check for mold before you feast — the bad ones go back.

scavenge.name: Salt block
scavenge.text: A dense block of salt. No calories, but everything you cook for the next month tastes like food again.

scavenge.name: Kola nuts
scavenge.text: Bitter red nuts, chewed for long days. Caffeine the old way — respect the dose.

scavenge.name: Sealed water sachet
scavenge.text: Plastic sachet of water, seal intact. The street vendors sold these by the thousand.

scavenge.name: Antimalarials (artemether)
scavenge.text: Foil blister pack, unbroken. For malaria fevers. Read the label, take the full course.

scavenge.name: Antiparasitic (mebendazole)
scavenge.text: Foil blister pack, unbroken. For worms and gut parasites. Only for those.

scavenge.name: Merchant's Seals
scavenge.text: A bundle of trade seals on a leather thong, worn smooth by thumbs.

scavenge.name: Uncharted Atlas
scavenge.text: An atlas of hand-drawn wells and crossings, annotated in three languages.

scavenge.name: Empty Pack
scavenge.text: A pack packed for a journey: everything folded, everything ready, never taken.

scavenge.name: Cache Fortress Kit
scavenge.text: A cache kit sealed against dust: tins, tools, and a list checked twice.

scavenge.name: Hatchet
scavenge.text: A hatchet hung by the back door, edge still keen. Made for splitting kindling — and for felling what needs felling.

challenge.description: Three seasons, each a boss: the hot steals your water, the wet drowns your stores and breeds fever, the cool is the only mercy. Stockpile, drain, endure.
challenge.name: The Monsoon

covers: Indian subcontinent: monsoon forest, groves, paddies and river ghats

feral orchard: Someone planted food here once. The trees remember.
mango grove: Old grafted trees. The fruit falls ripe.
river ghat: Still water. The pond is a pantry.

name: South Asia

ruins: A vegetable market, its stalls collapsed in rows. Pre-Burn. The weighing scales are still bolted to one counter — someone measured out their life here in kilos.
A government school, its classrooms open to the sky. Chalk dust still ghosts one blackboard: a half-erased lesson. The Burn took the wires; the walls kept standing out of spite.
A bus depot, the bays empty, one timetable still legible behind cracked glass. The routes outlived the buses.

scavenge.name: Sack of rice
scavenge.text: A torn sack, half-spilled. The grain inside is dry and clean — someone's winter, abandoned.

scavenge.name: Chef's Knife
scavenge.text: A chef's knife in a magnetic strip by the stove, honed by a thousand dinners. It remembers being a weapon's cousin.

scavenge.name: Riot gear
scavenge.text: A constable's riot kit behind the godown door. Heavy, hot, stops a boar.

scavenge.name: Bag of masoor dal
scavenge.text: Red lentils in a stitched jute bag. The stitching held; the weevils never found it.

scavenge.name: Tin of mustard oil
scavenge.text: A square tin, seal unbroken. Pungent, golden — cooking fat and lamp oil in one.

scavenge.name: Block of jaggery
scavenge.text: Dark unrefined sugar, wrapped in cloth. Ants found the corner; most of it is yours.

scavenge.name: Brick of tea
scavenge.text: Compressed black tea, stamped with a garden name. Morale in a brick.

scavenge.name: Pouch of turmeric
scavenge.text: Ground haldi in a sealed pouch. Stains everything; heals more.

scavenge.name: Tinned hilsa
scavenge.text: A tin of the queen of fish, in mustard oil. The label shows a river that still runs.

scavenge.name: Coil of coir rope
scavenge.text: Coconut-fiber rope, still strong. The old hands made everything from this.

scavenge.name: ORS packets
scavenge.text: Oral rehydration salts, foil-sealed. For dehydration and dysentery — mix with CLEAN water.

scavenge.name: Ciprofloxacin strips
scavenge.text: Foil strips, seal intact. For bacterial gut infections — the monsoon special. Read the label.

scavenge.name: Peace Accords
scavenge.text: A bound accord, signed in many inks, kept in the driest corner of the house.

scavenge.name: Universal Translator
scavenge.text: A phrasebook worn to softness, its margins full of corrections in two hands.

scavenge.name: Gilded Pack
scavenge.text: A pack with gilt clasps - someone's best, saved for an important road.

scavenge.name: Hatchet
scavenge.text: A hatchet hung by the back door, edge still keen. Made for splitting kindling — and for felling what needs felling.

name: The Steppe and the High Mountains

challenge.description: Early summer brings the meiyu — weeks of warm, unrelenting rain. The paddies flood, stored food molds, mosquitoes rise in clouds, and the rivers take back their roads.
challenge.name: The Plum Rains

seasons.note: Greens return. Bamboo shoots push up — the hungry season's exit.
The plum rains, then typhoon season. Hot, wet, everything grows — including the mosquitoes.
Harvest. Persimmons, chestnuts, rice. Fatten up.
The Siberian wind. Dry, bitter, still. Stored food or nothing.

covers: Eastern China, the Korean peninsula, Japan: bamboo brakes, feral rice paddies, persimmon orchards, tea terraces gone wild

bamboo brake: Where the poles stand thick, the shoots come up sweet.
chestnut lane: The burrs split in fall. Watch your fingers; the nuts are worth it.
feral paddy: The paddies went wild years ago. The rice didn't get the memo.
goji hedge: Thorny hedges, red berries. The birds know.
mulberry row: Silkworm country, once. The berries are for whoever's hungry now.
old orchard: Someone planted food here once. The trees remember.
pond margin: Still water, broad leaves standing tall. Dinner is under the mud.
tea terrace: Terraces gone to seed. The bushes still flush every spring.
temple ginkgo: Planted for shade and long life. The nuts are a bonus — roast them, and mind the dose.
wet ditch: Crisp corms under the mud. Cook them — the ditch water isn't clean.

name: East Asia

ruins: An elementary school. The classrooms are open to the sky; a wall chart of the seasons still hangs, faded to pastels. Someone chalked a height chart on a doorframe — the marks stop halfway up.

A township clinic. The medicine cabinet was emptied years ago, but the posters on the wall still explain hand-washing in four cheerful steps. The examination table is now a planter — mugwort grows through it.
A bus depot. The buses sit in a patient row, tires long since gone to moss. The route map by the gate is still legible: forty stops, none of which exist anymore.
A small roadside shrine, roofed and swept — someone still tends it. The offering box is empty, and stays empty.

scavenge.name: Instant noodles
scavenge.text: A brick of noodles, seasoning dust at the bottom of the bag. Civilization's emergency ration.

scavenge.name: Kitchen knife
scavenge.text: A kitchen knife in a bamboo block, the good heavy kind. Somebody's grandmother chopped a thousand dinners with this — it will chop other things.

scavenge.name: Camo Jacket
scavenge.text: A camo jacket folded in a cedar chest, quiet and broken-in. Hasn't been taken off since the sky changed, the tag jokes — the protection is no joke.

scavenge.name: Canned congee
scavenge.text: Rice porridge in a can. Bland, warm, perfect — the taste of being looked after.

scavenge.name: Rice cakes
scavenge.text: Pounded rice, dried hard. Soak it, grill it, soup it — it keeps coming back.

scavenge.name: Dried seaweed
scavenge.text: Nori sheets, still crisp. Salt and iodine in paper-thin form.

scavenge.name: Canned mackerel
scavenge.text: Oily fish in a tin. The bones went soft years ago; the flavor didn't.

scavenge.name: Soy sauce
scavenge.text: A heavy bottle, half full. Salt you can pour — everything bland becomes food again.

scavenge.name: Mooncakes (lotus)
scavenge.text: Dense, sweet, impossibly rich. A festival food, years out of season. Eat it anyway.

scavenge.name: Tea brick
scavenge.text: Compressed tea, hard as a roof tile. Not food — morale in solid form.

scavenge.name: Cold medicine (kakkonto)
scavenge.text: Foil packets of kakkonto — the kudzu-root cold formula. For fever and stiffness, not for infections.

scavenge.name: Bandages (roll)
scavenge.text: A clean roll, still sealed. For wounds that need covering.

scavenge.name: Field Surgeon's Satchel
scavenge.text: A surgeon's satchel, instruments rolled in oiled cloth, ready as the day it was packed.

scavenge.name: Everywhere Key
scavenge.text: A ring of keys labeled by door, the last one labeled simply: 'everywhere else.'

scavenge.name: Memory Seed Vault
scavenge.text: A lacquered box of seed packets, each dated, each named for a person.

scavenge.name: Hatchet
scavenge.text: A hatchet hung by the back door, edge still keen. Made for splitting kindling — and for felling what needs felling.
